w: Swamishri arrived in London at 10.25 am (4.23 am American Standard Time) at Heathrow Airport and reached the mandir late due to heavy traffic at 1.10 pm. After performing puja, Swamishri blessed the audience and then retired to bed.

While Swamishri was having lunch, a sadhu was giving details about the Nobel Peace Prize. Swamishri was listening attentively. However, at the drone of conversation among the gathering Swamishri told everyone, "If anyone wants to get it then listen carefully."
The sadhus responded, "We are praying that you get the Peace Prize."
"Having got Akshar Deri; that is the biggest Nobel Prize," Swamishri responded. "There is no need to pray for that. We have already got it."
"We are all praying that you get the prize," a sadhu added.
"I have already got it - Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. So I do not have any wish at all. I am in Akshardham ..."
Swamishri's reply had striking ring of absolute fulfillment and attainment of the Divine.
One who desires more than one's requirements invites miseries.

A person performs two types of karmas. One he does with evil intentions. That is, when he gives pain to others, persecutes them, troubles them or creates difficulties, he regresses and attains hell. And if he devotes himself to God and performs good actions, then he will be elevated.
Perform your worldly duties but do not forget God. Engage yourself in bhajan while anchored to the refuge of God for it will give you happiness, peace and success.
Swamishri performed murti-pratishtha of the canvas murtis of Guru Parampara in the mandir sanctum.
After his morning puja Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of murtis for hari mandirs in Acharda and Pandri villages (Surendranagar district and Limbdi sub-district respectively).

Guests : Hasan Kamal, Poet, Bahrain, praised, “Every column, every corner, every place made is really unique. It is hand made. A house takes more than two years to finish and this has been done in a very short period of time.”

Shri D.R. Kartikeyan, Former Director of CBI and Director General of Human Rights Commission, lauded, “If there is going to be an assessment on the 7 Wonders of the World, I think this complex is going to get the top most place. Every Indian should be proud of this. When you go around, it is just beautiful to look at and very entertaining. Every aspect of it imparts certain values of art and science of living a full life, harmonious life, spiritual life and a life full of harmony between various sects and groups of people all over the world.”
Abdul Hamid, Under Secretary, Bahrain, said, “Akshardham is so wonderful that it seems that aliens from another planet have come and made it. This is not a work of humans.”

Shri Balasubramaniam, Director of CBSE, praised, “I think it is a great spiritual monument which the city of Delhi should be proud of. It imbibes the basics of all religions, the immense wealth of our cultural heritage and the vibrancy of Indian thought. I think this kind of monument is required to make an impregnable impact on the younger generation of our country, who can really feel the mind and spirit of India.”

The annual gathering of past students who studied at the BAPS Gurukul in Gondal was held on the mandir grounds. More than 1,200 ex-students attended. The assembly commenced with reminiscences from past students. A drama, ‘Dream’, was enacted by the Gurukul boys. Then Mahant Swami gave awards to outstanding students of the Gurukul. This was followed by a traditional dance and offering of garlands to Swamishri. Another drama, ‘From Darkness to Light’, was performed by students of the Gurukul. Finally, Swamishri emphasized in his blessings about the need for values and understanding the glory of Yogiji Maharaj.
